welcome.subject: You're in
welcome.body:
{handle}, your invite to the Backroom went through. That is where the work is posted and where it is paid.

Open the Route map, pick The Backroom in your address book and connect. Log in with your invite and look at Contracts. Take the library job first. It is small and nobody is watching that machine.

I vouched for you. Don't make me regret it.

Wren

firstAccept.subject: How a job goes
firstAccept.body:
Good. Here is the shape of every job.

One. Disconnect from the Backroom. Your gateway holds one connection at a time.

Two. On the Route map, add a relay or two before you connect to the target. Every relay is one more step a trace has to follow, which is time for you. The Open Relay Registry lists more addresses.

Three. Connect. Break the password on the administrator account, then log in.

Four. Do what the contract says. Your Contract window shows when it is done.

Five. Open Logs, pick the lines that show your login and what you did, and scrub them. Then disconnect. If they read those lines later, they fine you.

Breaking in gets noticed. When the trace warning turns red, the number on it is how long you have. If it reaches you, it costs you. Leave early if you have to and go back in.

When the job is done, press Deliver in the Contract window. You get paid on the spot.

Wren

firstDelivery.subject: First one done
firstDelivery.body:
That is a first job delivered. More work shows on the board as your rating goes up.

Some systems put a proxy or a firewall in your way. A proxy stops you changing records and logs. A firewall stops you copying and deleting files. The Backroom's Market sells a bypass for each. Buy them when a job needs them, not before.

Two more things worth knowing. While a firewall bypass runs you can line up its ports by hand, which is much faster than waiting. And if a trace is closing in, pick a spare server on the Route map and reroute through it. That makes the trace start that step again.

Wren

paid.subject: Paid: {title}
paid.body:
Received. {pay} credits have been sent to your account through the Backroom.

We will not speak again.

contractFailed.subject: Contract withdrawn: {title}
contractFailed.body:
I hear {target} traced someone last night. I cannot be connected to that.

The contract is withdrawn. If it appears on the board again, it will be because I had no better option.

caught.subject: Heard you got traced
caught.body:
{target} followed you home. Word gets around.

They have fined you {fine} credits and changed their passwords, so whatever you had broken there is gone. The Backroom will not give you work for {hours} hours. Lie low, let the clock run, and come back.

Next time use more relays, and leave before the timer says you have to.

Wren

review.subject: They read their logs
review.body:
{target} went through its access log after you left and found {lines} that should not have been there. It was enough to put a name to.

They have fined you {fine} credits. No trace this time, so the Backroom still has work for you.

Before you disconnect, open Logs and scrub your login and anything that says a file was copied, deleted or a record changed. The lines that only say a connection opened or closed prove nothing.

Wren

harderSecurity.subject: Harder doors
harderSecurity.body:
{handle}, you have enough work behind you that the board will start showing you jobs with better locks on them. Two things you have not met yet.

Some monitors are quick, and the best start tracing the moment you connect. The Market now sells a Monitor Bypass. Run it from the security strip before you log in. While the monitor is blind, nothing you do is noticed and a trace that is already running stands still. It works once per connection and it does not last, so know what you are there to do before you start it. When it lands, you are shown the monitor's check-in pattern. Repeat it and you stay hidden longer. Get it wrong and you lose some of the time, so leave it alone if you did not catch it.

Some files are encrypted. You can copy one like any other, but you cannot read it and no client will pay for it until it is open. Buy the Decrypter and run it on the file from Programs, on your own gateway. It takes a while. It keeps working after you disconnect.

Wren

phishing.subject: People are the soft part
phishing.body:
{handle}, breaking a password is slow and loud. Asking for it is neither.

People hand things over to someone they trust who sounds like they belong. So when you are on a server, open the files and read them. Your gateway keeps a note of every person a file names and every detail worth repeating.

Then open Messages and press Write to someone. Pick who you are writing to and what you want from them. Pick whose name goes on it. It has to be somebody that person would do this for. Then pick up to three details that person would know. The right name with the right details gets you an answer in under an hour.

Get it wrong and they go quiet for a few hours. Get it wrong twice with the same person and they report it. Their side changes its passwords and the board hears about it.

Start at the Open Relay Registry. Its public files say more than they should about the people at Polar Mesh, and Polar Mesh has a strong password on its operator account.

Wren

phishRefused.subject: Re: {label}

phishReported.subject: You were reported
phishReported.body:
{name} did not believe your second message either, and this time they passed it up the line.

Their side has changed its passwords, so anything you had broken there is gone, and {name} will not answer you again. The board has heard, and your rating has taken the knock.

Read more before you write. The details have to be ones that person would know.

Wren
